notes: Swarm's budget checks (M4). Written by the Technical Director at stage 0, before the game exists: until tests/games/swarm/main.asm does, the runner reports SKIP. That file is the gameplay-engineer's, two lines: '#define AUTOPLAY' then '#import "games/swarm/src/main.asm"'. AUTOPLAY makes the game play the designer's worst case by itself (wave 12, scripted stick, nothing dies): docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#labels-the-game-must-provide lists what it does and every label these checks read. 'stage' is the M4 stage the game's code has reached (docs/milestones/M4-training-game.md, stages 1-5): the gameplay-engineer sets it at the start of each stage and changes nothing else here. Checks with a higher from_stage print PENDING. Units: raster cycles, DMA included, IRQs excluded for main-loop routines (engine/README.md#budget-units). Every game limit is an estimate until its stage measures it; a failing check is reported with the measured figure, and the Technical Director re-baselines. The per-routine limits add up to 6,720 for game_update (THE LONG RUN, 2026-10-03: player_update 365 -> 440, counted with a zone IRQ splitting it, and collide_update 2,825 -> 2,750, its placed worst frame 2,612 + 5%, so the sum is unchanged: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-5-review. STAGE 5, 2026-10-02: diver_update 2,020, it was 1,350: its own worst frame was placed and measured at 1,924, docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#row-6-the-divers and tests/games/swarm/stage5_diver_worst.py; the rest as re-set from stage 3's measurements, docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-3-measured: input 40; player_update 440 (365 until the long run: 150 CPU + the shot's sound request 51 counted as one short routine in the display in ONE piece, 358); pshot_update and stars_update 60 each; formation_update 750; diver_update 2,020; eshot_update 200; collide_update 2,750 (2,825 until the long run: 2,595 for the grid lookup as built + 224 counted for stage 4's sound requests, the player's hit twice, or the explosion once: never both); panel_update 250; 150 for the main loop itself; no separate allowance for sfx_play calls any more, each being inside its caller's limit), + 435 for the sound tick (measured; the 45 held for an eighth SID write is released: Simon listened at stage 4 and asked for no change) = 7,155 against the engine's 7,200: 45 of headroom, which the idle check enforces (670 until stage 5 with diver_update at 1,350 and the tick at 480; 650 with the tick estimated at 500, 625 before stage 3 was measured, 585 before that, and 935 before stage 2). THE SUM IS A CEILING NO FRAME REACHES: each row is its routine's own worst frame, and those frames need different states; the largest whole game_update found is 4,371 in a placed frame (stage5_diver_worst.txt, JX) and 3,758 sampled. STAGE 3 MEASURED (tests/games/swarm/stage3_costs.py, stage3_collide_worst.py and stage3_oneoff.py, results beside each): every limit here now rests on a measurement. THE SOUND IS MEASURED TOO, in the module's spike (tests/engine/sfx, locked): sfx_update 417 at worst (whole call 429), a game's tick IRQ 498, sfx_play 34/49/37 by path; what each of the game's nine requests costs where it is made is counted by tests/games/swarm/sfx_request_costs.py (results beside it) and decided in docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-4-part-b-sound-requests. STAGE 1 FIGURES CARRY NO DMA: with 3 sprites, game_update runs on raster lines 23-31, above the first badline (measured, docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-1-measured), so the display allowance (x 1.27) in every limit is untested until stage 2 puts the formation on screen. For that reason no limit here is re-baselined to a stage 1 measurement; each source line records the stage 1 figure beside the estimate. STAGE 2 PART A (formation, no collisions) was measured by tests/games/swarm/stage2a_costs.py, results beside it: still all above the first badline (docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-2-part-a-measured). STAGE 2 PART B (hits, explosions, score) was measured by tests/games/swarm/stage2b_costs.py, results beside it (docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-2-part-b-measured). SAMPLE COUNTS: a routine in the top border has a cost that depends only on its own state, so its count covers that state's cycle (stars 48 frames: 300; formation 192: 600); a routine in the display (player_update, collide_update, diver_update, game_update) lands on a different raster line every frame and the AUTOPLAY script repeats only after thousands of frames, so 600 samples are a look, not a proof: its limit is the counted worst case and make test-long is the longer look. WHAT AUTOPLAY CAN'T MEASURE (nothing dies in it) is measured on the game build with states set through the monitor, by a stageN_costs.py beside this file: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#what-autoplay-cannot-measure. A stage built in parts: memory-map.md#labels-the-game-must-provide, last paragraphs. warmup_frames 400: boot, the wave intro (50 frames since the tuning after the stage 4 playtest; 100 before) and the first launches; the game's own GAME_IDLE_WARMUP is 200 frames. The first memory check runs 3,000 more frames and the others read at that same moment (after_frames 0), except the stage 5 soak, which runs 10,000 more (about 13,600 frames in all). STAGE 5: 'stage' is 5 from the Technical Director's review (2026-10-02), so the four soak checks run. STAGE 4: 'stage' becomes 4 in the commit that wires the sound in (the four checks that start at stage 4 all need engine/sfx.asm's labels); waves and the title were measured before that by tests/games/swarm/stage4_costs.py (part A, no sound: stage4_costs.txt, stage4a_collide_worst.txt; memory-map.md#stage-4-part-a-measured). The part B checklist is memory-map.md#stage-4-part-b-sound-requests.

checks.name: player_update
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 3, #short-routines-in-the-display and #stage-5-review (the long run). RE-SET 2026-10-03 (Technical Director) after make test-long read 377 against 365: the count of 358 assumed the routine runs in one piece, and in the display a zone IRQ can land inside it. IRQ time is excluded, but the routine is then two pieces at two places in the frame, and each can meet a badline and its own lines' sprite fetches. COUNTED with one nested IRQ: 201 CPU (the dearest path: the flash, a move, a shot fired, its request replacing a pending enemy shot's, 49) in two pieces, a badline each, 8 sprites a line = 439 (short_routine_dma.py worst_split), so 440. MEASURED (tests/games/swarm/stage5_longrun_fails.py, results beside it): 150,000 passes of this build, 0 IRQs nested max 346, 1 IRQ (3,018 passes) max 390, 2 IRQs (18) max 351; every pass over 358 had one IRQ in it, and the long run's 377 is the 186-CPU path split on lines 58-60 / 63-68 across badlines 59 and 67 with 6 sprites a line (the model's figure for that case is 377 exactly); with the dearest request forced in every firing frame, 120,000 passes: 397 at most (one IRQ, 7 sprites a line; no IRQ 357, inside the one-piece count of 358). NOT COVERED: two nested IRQs can in principle give three pieces, 520 by the same count; seen 31 times in 270,000 passes, never over 366. A reading over 440 is that case. History: 365 from stage 4 (150 CPU + the shot's request = 201 CPU, counted in one piece: 358, 7 spare), 290 at stage 3, 200 before. Raster cycles, IRQs excluded. Stage 3 measured 92-260 in this build; tuned, with the request, 302-326 sampled; make test-long (x34) 92-377, average 134.9
